chunks: From him, from Abdul Rahman ibn Hammad al-Kufi, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Giffari, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who consoles the poor from his wealth, and is fair with the people from himself, so he is a true Believer.'

key_terms.وَاسَى: To console or provide financial aid

ai.seo_question: What are the key characteristics of a true believer according to this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni links this narration to the chapter on justice, highlighting Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) emphasis on 'wasā' (financial support/consolation) as a tangible act of faith. The hadith underscores that true Iman is manifested not just in belief, but in equitable self-assessment and generous provision for the needy, reflecting the Shia concept of 'Adl (justice) extending to social and economic spheres.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Abdul Rahman Bin Hammad Al Kufy, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim Al Ghiffary, from Ja’far Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who consoles the poor one from his wealth, and is fair with the people from himself, so he is a true Momin (Believer)’.
en.sarwar: 17. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad al-Kufi from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Ghifari from Ja’far ibn Ibrahim al-Ja’fari from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘
Whoever comforts the poor with his property and yields to justice for people against his own soul indeed is a believer.”
